text: A voice call sends a 160-byte payload every 20 ms over Ethernet with IP, UDP and RTP headers. Roughly what fraction of the wire time is overhead?
explanation: 160 bytes of payload rides inside 238 bytes on the wire (20 bytes gap and preamble, 18 Ethernet header and FCS, 40 bytes of IP+UDP+RTP). Efficiency is 160/238 = 67%, so about a third is overhead. This is why 'calls per circuit' is never the codec bitrate divided into the link rate.
